description: Add a name for tracked emails to use for the open pixel and for links: a subdomain of a domain you send from, like t.acme.com. Add one for each domain you send from, so each email's links point at the domain it was sent from. A whole domain, like acme.com or acme.com.br, is refused (400 trackingDomainNeedsSubdomain), because DNS allows no CNAME record there. Adding a name you already have answers that domain as it stands. A workspace can have up to 10 (past that, 409 trackingDomainLimit). The answer names the CNAME record to create in that domain's DNS, and `dnsHost` says which DNS provider holds it (as list_tracking_domains describes). The domain starts pending and is verified once the record points at its target: we check every hour, or when you call check_tracking_domain. This needs setup permission, or manage for a signed-in admin or owner. A campaign tracks opens only when its trackOpens is on, and clicks only when its trackClicks is on. Tracking can hurt delivery: some spam filters treat a tracking image or rewritten links as a sign of bulk mail. Call check_tracking_domain first. If the check is unanswered, retry without changing DNS. Otherwise, publish the CNAME from `records` only if it is missing or wrong, using its `name` (or `nameInZone` inside the known zone) and `value`. Keep it DNS only at Cloudflare, never proxied. We never take a DNS password or token.

hostname.description: A name under a domain you own, used only for tracking, like t.acme.com. A pasted URL is cut to its host.

idempotencyKey.description: Your own id for this one call, such as a UUID, up to 255 characters. If the call fails with no answer, call again with the same key and the same arguments: within 24 hours, a saved answer comes back instead of a second run. A call left unanswered can run again after 15 minutes, so a send also keeps its intentKey or draft revision.
